newsitem.title: UK: Auctioneers Sotheby's probes smuggling allegations.
newsitem.headline: Auctioneers Sotheby's probes smuggling allegations.

text.p: British auctioneers Sotheby's said on Thursday it has suspended senior staff after allegations that it had broken the law by smuggling art treasures from Italy to Britain.
George Bailey, managing director of Sotheby's Europe, said he was taking the allegations made in an investigative television programme seriously and was conducting an investigation.

"It's an isolated case...I've gone out and taken action. I am holding an inquriy and once I have information I will take the necessary action to implement those rules and regulations that have been broken," he told BBC radio.

But Bailey said he deplored the method of entrapment that he claimed the "Dispatches" programme used when it filmed Sotheby's staff in Milan with a hidden camera. The programme is due to be screened on Britain's Channel 4 television on Thursday night.

The programme is expected to show evidence of Sotheby's Old Masters expert in Milan offering to smuggle a painting by Italian artist Giusseppe Nogari to Britain and apparently admitting that it was illegal for the portrait to leave Italy.
Another senior Sotheby's employee in London is filmed being given the painting.

The investigative programme was based on a book by arts journalist Peter Watson which claims Sotheby's arranged the illegal exports of valuable paintings from Italy and India to England and created false papers to conceal the origin of other art treasures.

"We bought a painting, an Old Master, in Italy and we took it into Sotheby's Milan office and they offered to smuggle it for us to London and they did. They organised the whole thing...they gave us instructions to set up a false address in London, which we did," Watson told the BBC.
"The painting was delivered. We took it into Sotheby's. It came up for auction and we bought it back and returned it to Italy where it belonged," he added.
Watson claimed he had evidence that such practices were going on for a long time and that it was a widespread activity -- the export of protected art treasures from countries.
He added that his investigation was a closely supervised operation.
